question: ABCD is a quadrilateral in which AB ∥ DC. E and F are the midpoints of the diagonals AC and BD, respectively. If AB = 18 cm and CD = 6 cm, then EF = ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a trapezium ABCD where AB ∥ DC, the distance between the midpoints of the diagonals AC and BD is given by the formula:

Length of EF = ½ × |AB − CD|

Given AB = 18 cm and CD = 6 cm.

EF = ½ × (18 − 6) = ½ × 12 = 6 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Quadrilateral ABCD is a trapezium with AB ∥ DC.

Length of parallel side AB = 18 cm.

Length of parallel side CD = 6 cm.

E is the midpoint of diagonal AC and F is the midpoint of diagonal BD.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/64ba4da1d15df4de1e458b979af35109d200c279ca30bd431039282d6638177e.png] 

**Formula Used:**

For a trapezium with parallel sides a and b, the segment joining the midpoints of the diagonals is parallel to the bases and has length |a − b| / 2.

**Calculations:**

⇒ Parallel sides are AB = 18 cm and CD = 6 cm.

⇒ E and F are midpoints of diagonals AC and BD respectively.

⇒ EF = ½ × (AB − CD)

⇒ EF = ½ × (18 − 6)

⇒ EF = ½ × 12

⇒ EF = 6 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 6 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Median of a Trapezium

The line segment joining the midpoints of the non-parallel sides (legs) is called the median. Its length is the average of the parallel sides: Median = (AB + CD) / 2.

Area of a Trapezium

The area of a trapezium is calculated as Area = ½ × (sum of parallel sides) × height, where height is the perpendicular distance between the parallel sides.

Isosceles Trapezium Property

In an isosceles trapezium, the non-parallel sides are equal in length, the base angles are equal, and the diagonals are equal (AC = BD).

Cyclic Quadrilateral

An isosceles trapezium is always a cyclic quadrilateral, meaning all its vertices lie on a single circle.</p
